messages:
samir: Hey — running `terraform apply` for infra branch and TF wants to update ConfigMap `model-flags` in kube even though I didn't change the CM YAML in git. Plan shows only an annotation change: `metadata.annotations["checksum/config"]` new value. Anyone seen this?

jess: Which CM file / path is this? is it the per-model flags config under apps/models/configs?

samir: Yes: apps/models/configs/configmap-model-flags.yaml in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789. Kube `kubectl get cm model-flags -o yaml` shows the same data block as the file in the repo. TF plan only wants to update the checksum annotation.

lyn: Could be ordering or whitespace differences used to compute the checksum. Can you paste the `kubectl get cm ... -o yaml` and `terraform state show kubernetes_config_map.model_flags` (or the `data.template_file` sha if that's how it's computed)?

samir: Pasted snippets:
```
# kubectl get cm model-flags -o yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: model-flags
  annotations:
    checksum/config: "9a1b2c3d"
data:
  tiny-model: "enabled"
  big-model: "disabled"
```

and TF state excerpt:

```
metadata.0.annotations.%": 1
metadata.0.annotations.checksum/config = "7b2d1e8f"
```

So TF sees `7b2...`, cluster has `9a1...` even though `data` matches.

maria: We stamp checksums via a pipeline step when rendering k8s manifests (so deployments pick up config changes). If the checksum source differs (ordering, trailing newline), you'll get mismatch even if semantic data is same.

tom: Also check the provider version and whether TF is canonicalizing the `data` map deterministically. I remember provider `2.x` had map ordering nondeterminism in some cases that affected computed diffs.

samir: Using provider `hashicorp/kubernetes v2.11.0`. I tried `sha256sum` on the rendered file and it matched the cluster dump at first glance. Then I ran `yq -S` (sort keys) and re-computed sha; now TF and cluster sha match. So it looks like ordering differences in the file generation caused a different checksum.

jess: Good catch. Action: ensure we canonicalize the CM YAML before computing the checksum in the pipeline and in TF locals. Quick check: add `yq -S` to the CI step that creates the checksum and to the local dev script.

lyn: For immediate remediation: if the plan only updates the annotation (no data change) and you validated the canonicalized sha, `terraform apply` will sync the annotation and no behavioral change to the CM. You can also just manually patch the annotation to match TF, but better to fix generator.

samir: Verified in staging: did an `apply` and it updated the annotation to `7b2d1e8f` and the deployment rolled as expected. `kubectl rollout status` returned ok. No config data changed.

maria: Long-term: add a unit in the pipeline that canonicalizes the YAML before computing checksum and fails the build if generated file differs only by ordering/whitespace. I'll open a tiny RFC.

tom: I'll add a tiny CI job (scripts/ci/canonicalize-cm.sh) that runs `yq -S` and computes `sha256sum` and compares to the value used by TF. If mismatch, fail and surface the offending files and diff.

jess: Also add a note in infra/README.md under "ConfigMap checksum" about canonicalization and which `yq` flags to use. Saves future head-scratching.

samir: Sounds good. I pushed a small fix to the generator to strip extra trailing newline and to sort keys before hashing — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/790. Will monitor staging apply then promote.

tom: Nice. We should also check any other configmaps generated by the templater.

samir: Yep running grep now. Will open follow-up if I find others. Thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: applied terraform in staging at 1820000345 by samir — plan included annotation update only, no data changes.

samir: Closing loop — patch merged, CI job queued, will watch prod promote after tomorrow's maintenance window. Ping me if you see similar diffs.
